result.journal: ACM Trans. Multim. Comput. Commun. Appl.
result.keywords: This article examines how deep features and event-aware control strategies can improve adaptive bitrate (ABR) streaming in modern multimedia players. We survey recent approaches that combine network throughput estimation, user-event responsiveness, and multimedia event recognition to optimize quality-of-experience (QoE) under fluctuating bandwidth, startup, seek, and low-latency live-streaming conditions. In addition to reviewing representative ABR algorithms and deep-learning-based event analysis methods, we present a comparative experimental framework for evaluating bitrate stability, rebuffering, and responsiveness across video and audio-driven streaming scenarios. The discussion highlights benchmark datasets, practical deployment constraints, and emerging directions for integrating learned event cues into DASH-style reference players and related adaptive streaming systems.
result.title: Learning Event-Aware Bitrate Control in Adaptive Multimedia Players: A Survey and Experimental Study
